newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end down on holiday mood.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end down on holiday mood.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended down on Thursday, with institutions seen retreating from the market and wait-and-see sentiment prevailing ahead of the Hong Kong handover holiday, brokers said.

The Shanghai B index fell 1.328 points or 1.59 percent to 82.129 on volume of 29.799 million shares, while the Shenzhen B index lost 0.73 points or 0.50 percent to 143.80 as turnover shrank to HK$67 million from Wednesday's HK$77 million.
"Some institutions have been pulling out of the market ahead of the handover, which has for a long time served as an excuse for them to push up share prices," an analyst said.
"The handover will soon be history and the market is waiting for new trading incentives," he said.
The Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges will be closed on June 30 and July 1 to mark Hong Kong's return to Chinese control. Trading will resume on Wednesday, July 2.
"Foreign securities firms were seen unwinding positions and taking profit (in the Shanghai market)," said one local broker.
"The return of Hong Kong has been regarded as the main positive news supporting the market, but with the day fast approaching the event has already been digested," he added.
With market sentiment weak, investors bought shares in newly listed Hainan Airlines Co Ltd, which drained liquidity out of the overall market, they said.
Hainan Airlines was both the most actively traded Shanghai B share counter and the top gainer, ending at $0.536, up $0.066 or 14.04 percent from its issue price of $0.470 yuan.
There had been talk in the market that Beijing would introduce new measures in July to further depress stock speculation, brokers in Shenzhen said.

"Investors are slicing their holdings before the holiday because they are concerned that Beijing might announce some negative market-moving news after the Hong Kong handover," an analyst with China Guotai Securities said.
Shenzhen Petrochemical was the worst Shenzhen B share performer, falling HK$0.20 or 6.67 percent to HK$2.80.
Brokers in Shanghai said they expected Shanghai A and B shares to fall further on Friday.
"With uncertainties for the market after the Hong Kong handover, most investors have little interest in building new positions," one broker said.
The Shanghai A index fell 13.521 points or one percent to 1,343.199 points on volume of 370.721 million shares worth 5.1 billion yuan.
But the SSE30 blue chip index bucked the trend to edge up 0.983 points or 0.02 percent to 4,137.604 points, boosted by selective buying.

The Shenzhen A share index slipped 3.12 points or 0.67 percent to 460.09 as new listings diverted some "hot money" from existing shares, brokers said. Turnover reached 9.4 billion yuan, compared with 9.2 billion yuan in the previous session.
Seven companies listed a combined 340 million A shares in Shenzhen on Thursday, a record number of new company listings on the south China bourse in one day, brokers said.
They all posted strong debuts, which attracted many investors seeking quick profits, they said.
New listings are not calculated into indices on their first day of trading.
